title: Drumming: Rudiments, Mechanics & Rhythm Theory
source: PAS International Drum Rudiments & Percussion Pedagogy
scope: Rudiments, stick technique, polyrhythms, and coordination

cards.prompt: What is the sticking pattern for an inward (or delayed) paradiddle?
options: R L L R L R R L
R L R R L R L L
R L R L L R L R
R R L R L L R L
cards.answer: R L L R - L R R L (Inward Paradiddle).
cards.elaboration: Unlike the standard single paradiddle (R L R R), the inward inversion places the double stroke immediately after the initial lead tap.

cards.prompt: In Moeller technique, what is the core mechanical motion of the 'whip' stroke?
options: Leading from the elbow/forearm with the wrist following like a whip
Locking the wrist and driving solely from the shoulder
Squeezing tightly between thumb and index fulcrum
Using exclusively pinky-finger rebound
cards.answer: Leading with the forearm and elbow, allowing the wrist and stick to whip downward effortlessly.
cards.elaboration: Sanford Moeller modeled this on military drummers; relaxed arm whip generates high volume with minimal muscular fatigue.

cards.prompt: What distinguishes a Flam Accent from a Flam Tap?
options: Flam Accent is grouped in triplets (lR-L-R); Flam Tap is grouped in duplets (lR-R)
Flam Accent uses double strokes; Flam Tap uses only single strokes
Flam Accent is played only on the snare rim
Flam Tap alternates hands while Flam Accent never alternates
cards.answer: Flam Accents are 3-note groupings (lR-L-R rL-R-L); Flam Taps are 2-note double groupings (lR-R rL-L).
cards.elaboration: Mastering both gives you the building blocks for fluent syncopated fills across compound and simple meters.

cards.prompt: What rhythmic mnemonic accurately represents a 3 against 2 polyrhythm (3 over 2)?
options: 'Not dif-fi-cult' (Together - Right - Left - Right)
‘Pass the god-damned butter’
‘What would Jesus do’
‘Pea-nut but-ter jel-ly’
cards.answer: 'Not dif-fi-cult' (Beat 1 together, beat 2 of triplet, beat 2 of duplet).
cards.elaboration: In numbers: 1, 2-and, 3; the duplet hits on 1 and the midpoint between beats 2 and 3 of the triplet.

options: A groove where no two limbs (hands or feet) strike simultaneously
A groove played in strict straight 4/4 without syncopation
A groove where the hi-hat never stops playing 16th notes
A continuous roll from the snare to the lowest floor tom
cards.answer: A groove where no two limbs hit at the exact same instant.
cards.elaboration: Pioneered by drummers like David Garibaldi and Steve Gadd, linear patterns produce crisp, articulate funk textures.

cards.prompt: What is the primary difference between an American, German, and French timpani/drum grip?
options: Palm angle relative to the drum head (French palms face each other, German palms flat down, American ~45°)
The distance between the thumb and index finger only
Whether the stick is held with the right hand or left hand
Whether traditional grip is used on the weak hand
cards.answer: Palm angle: French is thumbs-up (90° vertical), German is palms flat (0° horizontal), American is halfway (~45°).
cards.elaboration: French grip favors rapid finger control; German grip maximizes wrist power; American blends both for drum set versatility.

cards.prompt: In half-time shuffle grooves (like Bernard Purdie or Jeff Porcaro's Rosanna shuffle), where do ghost notes typically sit?
options: On the unaccented inner partials of the underlying triplet grid
Directly on quarter-note downbeats 1, 2, 3, 4
Only on beats 2 and 4 directly behind the backbeat
Exclusively on the offbeat eighth notes
cards.answer: On the inner partials of the triplet grid, tucked softly between the main pulse notes.
cards.elaboration: The Purdie shuffle relies on delicate snare ghost notes occupying the middle partial of the triplet for its buoyant pocket.

cards.prompt: How is a Drag (or Ruff) technically executed in standard percussion notation?
options: Two grace notes played by the same hand rapidly preceding an accented primary note
A single grace note played open before the downbeat
A four-stroke single roll played over the barline
A continuous press roll terminated with a rimshot
cards.answer: Two soft grace notes (usually doubled by one hand) immediately leading into the primary accented note (llR or rrL).
cards.elaboration: The drag provides rhythmic snap and weight to classical orchestral pieces, march cadences, and funk ghost-note patterns.
